title: Village Greek Salad with a Feta Slab
summary: A classic village-style Greek salad piled with crunchy raw vegetables, briny olives and capers, topped with thick slabs of feta rather than crumbled in. Salting the tomatoes first and dressing everything just before serving keeps it fresh and far from watery.
equipment: colander set over a large bowl

ingredients.item: ripe tomatoes, cored, cut into wedges and the wedges halved
fine sea salt or table salt
dried oregano, plus a pinch for the feta
cucumber (about 350 g), quartered lengthwise and cut into 2 cm chunks
green pepper (about 150 g), deseeded and cut into thin rings or strips
block of feta, cut into 2 thick slabs

steps.title: Drain the tomatoes
steps.text: Toss the tomato pieces with ¼ tsp of the salt and tip them into the colander set over the bowl, then leave for 20-30 minutes. The salt pulls out the watery juice by osmosis, so the finished salad stays crisp instead of turning into a puddle. Discard the juice once it has collected.

steps.title: Soak the onion
steps.text: While the tomatoes drain, put the sliced onion into a small bowl with the cider vinegar and leave for 15 minutes. The acid softens the sharp, sulphurous bite of raw onion so it adds crunch without overpowering everything else. Lift the onion out once it's ready and set it aside.

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Stir the remaining a pinch of salt, the oregano and the pepper into the vinegar left behind from the onion, then whisk in 3 tbsp of the olive oil. Whisking briskly brings the oil and vinegar together into a dressing that clings to the vegetables rather than pooling at the bottom. It should look cloudy and well combined.

steps.title: Toss the salad
steps.text: In the now-empty large bowl, gently toss the drained tomatoes, soaked onion, cucumber, green pepper, olives and capers with the dressing. Go easy with the extra salt here, since the olives and the feta to come are already salty. A light hand keeps the vegetables intact rather than bruised.

steps.title: Top with feta and serve
steps.text: Pile the dressed vegetables onto the platter, lay the feta slabs on top, and sprinkle them with a pinch of oregano before drizzling over the last 1 tbsp of oil. Serving the feta whole rather than crumbled lets it stay creamy in the middle while the oil pools attractively around it. Bring it to the table and serve straight away.

tips: Skipping the tomato-salting step is the most common mistake here — it leaves the salad swimming in juice, so give it the full 20-30 minutes even if you're in a hurry.
Use tomatoes at room temperature for the best flavour; chilled tomatoes taste noticeably flatter.
Dress the vegetables only just before serving so the cucumber and pepper keep their crunch.
Taste before adding extra salt — olives, capers and feta all bring their own saltiness.
storage: This salad is best eaten fresh. If there are leftovers, cover and refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 1 day, as the vegetables will continue to soften and release liquid; it isn't suitable for freezing.
